refactorings.summary: The README file would significantly benefit from improved formatting, structural organization, and consistency. The main opportunities include proper markdown formatting for code blocks, better visual hierarchy, extraction of content into separate documentation files, and clearer separation of concerns. The changes would transform this from raw instructional text into professional documentation.

recommendations.description: Implement proper markdown formatting for all code blocks and commands. Currently commands and descriptions are concatenated without clear separation or syntax highlighting. Use ```bash...``` code blocks to properly format shell commands and their output.

Add clear section headers and organize content hierarchically. The README should have markdown headers (# Getting Started, ## Prerequisites, ## Installation, etc.) to provide navigation structure and improve readability.

Document platform-specific variations for file paths. The instructions use Unix-style paths (~/Hello-World) without acknowledging Windows (C:\Users\) or other platform differences. Add platform-specific examples or use generic path notation.

Add error handling and troubleshooting guidance. If commands fail, users won't know what went wrong. Document common errors (e.g., 'Directory already exists', 'Permission denied') and their solutions.

Improve consistency in formatting and terminology. Descriptions should be separate from commands, and explanations should be clear and consistent in style. Consider adding inline code comments to clarify command purposes.
Add trailing newline to end of file. The file currently ends without a newline character, which is considered best practice for text files in Unix-like systems.
